A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gradient-regularization research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLHF experiments on TL;DR and AlpacaFarm, reasoning experiments on GSM8K and MATH, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds implementation ablations and runtime comparisons in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed finite-difference GR procedure, action reuse, gradient clipping, and transformer-only perturbations are unchanged. The new ablations test alternatives without changing the adopted method.

E1.justification: Both versions use TL;DR, AlpacaFarm, GSM8K, and MATH with the same task coverage. The added ablations and runtime measurements use existing tasks; the stronger-judge experiments already appeared in v1 Appendix D.3.

E2.justification: New Tables 10–11 explicitly compare default GR with importance-sampling-corrected action reuse, action resampling, and perturbing all parameters. Comparator membership in the original benchmark comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.6 adds Pythia 1B TL;DR ablations across four GR strengths, and D.7 adds walltime-to-early-stopping evaluation for Qwen2.5-1.5B on AlpacaFarm. Existing benchmark splits and training settings are retained; the KL implementation clarification is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Appendix D.6 adds targeted tests of whether action reuse needs correction or resampling and whether perturbations should include embeddings and output heads. D.7 adds computational-efficiency analysis. The existing judge, hyperparameter, reset-schedule, and reward-hacking analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly reports three-seed means and standard deviations for the 0.5B GSM8K experiments; v1 gives point estimates without this information. This establishes new reporting, not an explicit increase from a stated earlier run count. D.6 specifies one seed per new ablation.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces the 0.5B results with three-seed summaries: for example, LLM-judge No Reg changes from 2.0% to 20.7 ± 3.8%, and rule-based GR from 50.9% to 56.2 ± 1.0%. These are changed aggregates, not demonstrated method improvements. Tables 10–12 add ablation and runtime results; the 1.5B GSM8K values and Tables 1, 2, and 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, propositions, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices B and E are unchanged. The expanded limitations do not introduce a new formal assumption, proof, or counterexample.

C1.justification: The title changes 'Prevents' to 'Mitigates.' The abstract replaces the assertion that Reference Resets implicitly use GR with an empirical statement that they find flatter regions with higher reward accuracy. The principal contributions and conclusion remain.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's existing caveats, v2 explains how strict answer formatting could violate reward continuity and how flat incorrect maxima could make GR cause hacking and gradient-norm monitoring misleading. Appendix D.6 also adds interpretations concerning action-reuse bias, resampling variance, and embedding-perturbation instability.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds an implementation repository link. Appendix C.2 clarifies that the KL penalty enters the loss rather than the reward; D.6 specifies importance-ratio clipping to [0.5, 1.5], and D.7 identifies hardware for the runtime comparison. One pseudocode backward-call typo is corrected.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Appendix A are retained. Reference URL replacements, removals, and bibliographic wording edits do not add or remove research works or revise the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized title, abstract, grammar, and publication-header edits, adds a limitations paragraph and two appendix subsections, and renumbers the retained reward-hacking example. Most prose and the overall organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–12, adjusts Table 3 for uncertainty reporting, and changes Figure 5's marker styling. New main-text Figure 9 redraws the existing judge comparison, which remains in the appendix as Figure 14. Other changes mainly involve reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence for existing implementation choices, uncertainty reporting for the 0.5B GSM8K results, and measured runtime comparisons. The code pointer, implementation clarification, and more explicit failure conditions improve reproducibility and claim calibration. These are bounded gains: the new design ablations use one seed each, while the central method, theory, and benchmark coverage remain unchanged.
